## 2. Feature Description ✅<!--dv-evidence:-->

_Provenance: documented specification facts only; sources are linked from the heading indicator._


### Purpose

-  UART core provides serial communication capabilities for communication with modem or other external devices. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Peer types include modem or other external devices over serial link.
-  Core is designed to be maximally compatible with the industry standard National Semiconductors 16550A device. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Industry standard reference device is 16550A.
### Interface

-  Core provides WISHBONE slave interface for register access and data transfer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Used for UART control and data register access as responder to interconnect.
-  Serial communication uses RS232 protocol over a serial cable to external devices. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - External peers include modem or another computer.
  - Serial signals are STX_PAD_O output and SRX_PAD_I input.
-  Modem control register allows transferring control signals to a modem connected to the UART. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Control outputs include DTR and RTS.
  - Status inputs include DSR, CTS, RI and DCD.
-  Core provides optional BAUD_O output. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Output is an optional baud-rate related signal.
### Mode

-  Core supports only the FIFO mode of 16550 operation. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Standard 16550 operation is otherwise followed.
-  In loopback mode transmitter shift register output is internally connected to receiver shift register input. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Loopback is controlled by modem control register.
  - Modem loopback maps DTR to DSR, RTS to CTS, Out1 to RI and Out2 to DCD.
### Data Path

-  In loopback mode serial output STX_PAD_O is set to logic 1. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Serial output is held idle while internal loopback path carries data.
-  Upon reset receiver and transmitter FIFOs are cleared. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Ensures empty FIFO state before initialization.
-  Upon reset receiver and transmitter shift registers are cleared. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Clears in-progress serial bits in both directions.
### Interrupt

-  Upon reset all interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Interrupts remain disabled until enabled during initialization.
  - Interrupt output signal is INT_O.

### FIFO Control (FCR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 2 | Width: 8 | Access: W | Reset: 11000000b

#### Description

Control FIFO options

Configuration identification  📄<!--dv-sources:--> NEEDS_REVIEW: Register selects FIFO trigger level threshold which is a configuration threshold.
> Specification evidence: The FCR allows selection of the FIFO trigger level (the number of bytes in FIFO required
to enable the Received Data Available interrupt).

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | W | - | Ignored (Used to enable FIFOs in NS16550D). Since this UART only supports FIFO mode, this bit is ignored. | - |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 1 |  | W | - | Writing a ‘1’ to bit 1 clears the Receiver FIFO and resets its logic. But it doesn’t clear the shift register, i.e. receiving of the current character continues. | - |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 2 |  | W | - | Writing a ‘1’ to bit 2 clears the Transmitter FIFO and resets its logic. The shift register is not cleared, i.e. transmitting of the current character continues. | - |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5-3 |  | W | - | Ignored | - |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 7-6 |  | W | - | Define the Receiver FIFO Interrupt trigger level | 00 = 1 byte; 01 = 4 bytes; 10 = 8 bytes; 11 = 14 bytes |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

<!--dv-register-detail-end-->

<!--dv-register-detail:0966030f7f5930b2-->
### Interrupt Identification (IIR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 2 | Width: 8 | Access: R | Reset: C1h

#### Description

Get interrupt information

Configuration identification  📄<!--dv-sources:--> NEEDS_REVIEW: Status register for retrieving highest priority pending interrupt, not a configuration control.
> Specification evidence: The IIR enables the programmer to retrieve what is the current highest priority pending
interrupt.

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Bit 0 | - | - | Indicates that an interrupt is pending when logic ‘0’; no interrupt pending when ‘1’. | 0 = An interrupt is pending; 1 = No interrupt is pending |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 3-1 | Bit 3 Bit 2 Bit 1 | - | - | Identifies the current highest priority pending interrupt type, priority, source and reset control. | 0 1 1 = 1st Receiver Line Status - Parity, Overrun or Framing errors or Break Interrupt - Reading the Line Status Register; 0 1 0 = 2nd Receiver Data available - FIFO trigger level reached - FIFO drops below trigger level; 1 1 0 = 2nd Timeout Indication - There’s at least 1 character in the FIFO but no character has been input to the FIFO or read from it for the last 4 Char times. - Reading from the FIFO (Receiver Buffer Register); 0 0 1 = 3rd Transmitter Holding Register empty - Transmitter Holding Register Empty - Writing to the Transmitter Holding Register or reading IIR.; 0 0 0 = 4th Modem Status - CTS, DSR, RI or DCD. - Reading the Modem status register. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5-4 | Bits 4 and 5 | - | - | Logic ‘0’. | 0 = Logic ‘0’ |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 7-6 | Bits 6 and 7 | - | - | Logic ‘1’ for compatibility reason. | 1 = Logic ‘1’ for compatibility reason |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

<!--dv-register-detail-end-->

<!--dv-register-detail:46c60da3fc4c938d-->
### Line Control Register (LCR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 3 | Width: 8 | Access: RW | Reset: 00000011b

#### Description

Control connection

Configuration identification  📄<!--dv-sources:--> NEEDS_REVIEW: Controls line control format parameters such as data bits, parity and stop bits
> Specification evidence: Set the Line Control Register to the desired line control parameters.

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-0 | Select number of bits in each character | RW | - | Select number of bits in each character | 00 = 5 bits; 01 = 6 bits; 10 = 7 bits; 11 = 8 bits |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 2 | Specify the number of generated stop bits | RW | - | Specify the number of generated stop bits. Note that the receiver always checks the first stop bit only. | 0 = 1 stop bit; 1 = 1.5 stop bits when 5-bit character length selected and 2 bits otherwise |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 3 | Parity Enable | RW | - | Parity Enable | 0 = No parity; 1 = Parity bit is generated on each outgoing character and is checked on each incoming one. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 4 | Even Parity select | RW | - | Even Parity select | 0 = Odd number of ‘1’ is transmitted and checked in each word (data and parity combined). In other words, if the data has an even number of ‘1’ in it, then the parity bit is ‘1’.; 1 = Even number of ‘1’ is transmitted in each word. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5 | Stick Parity bit. | RW | - | Stick Parity bit. | 0 = Stick Parity disabled; 1 = If bits 3 and 4 are logic ‘1’, the parity bit is transmitted and checked as logic ‘0’. If bit 3 is ‘1’ and bit 4 is ‘0’ then the parity bit is transmitted and checked as ‘1’. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 6 | Break Control bit | RW | - | Break Control bit | 1 = the serial out is forced into logic ‘0’ (break state).; 0 = break is disabled |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 7 | Divisor Latch Access bit. | RW | - | Divisor Latch Access bit. | 1 = The divisor latches can be accessed; 0 = The normal registers are accessed |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

<!--dv-register-detail-end-->

### Line Status (LSR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 5 | Width: 8 | Access: R | Reset: not stated

#### Description

Status information

Status
Register

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Data Ready (DR) indicator | R | - | Data Ready (DR) indicator. | 0 = No characters in the FIFO; 1 = At least one character has been received and is in the FIFO. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 1 | Overrun Error (OE) indicator | R | - | Overrun Error (OE) indicator | 1 = If the FIFO is full and another character has been received in the receiver shift register. If another character is starting to arrive, it will overwrite the data in the shift register but the FIFO will remain intact. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No overrun state |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 2 | Parity Error (PE) indicator | R | - | Parity Error (PE) indicator | 1 = The character that is currently at the top of the FIFO has been received with parity error. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No parity error in the current character |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 3 | Framing Error (FE) indicator | R | - | Framing Error (FE) indicator | 1 = The received character at the top of the FIFO did not have a valid stop bit. Of course, generally, it might be that all the following data is corrupt. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No framing error in the current character |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 4 | Break Interrupt (BI) indicator | R | - | Break Interrupt (BI) indicator | 1 = A break condition has been reached in the current character. The break occurs when the line is held in logic 0 for a time of one character (start bit + data + parity + stop bit). In that case, one zero character enters the FIFO and the UART waits for a valid start bit to receive next character. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No break condition in the current character |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5 | Transmit FIFO is empty. | R | - | Transmit FIFO is empty. | 1 = The transmitter FIFO is empty. Generates Transmitter Holding Register Empty interrupt. The bit is cleared when data is being been written to the transmitter FIFO.; 0 = Otherwise |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 6 | Transmitter Empty indicator. | R | - | Transmitter Empty indicator. | 1 = Both the transmitter FIFO and transmitter shift register |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

<!--dv-register-detail-end-->

### RTLOBS-e70fdc1b2e — reset ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

MSR delta clear uses self-clearing msi_reset: reset-initialized to 1, auto-cleared to 0, and re-asserted on msr_read to gate MSR delta field to zero.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived from always block sensitive to posedge clk/posedge wb_rst_i that sets msi_reset to 1 on wb_rst_i, to 0 when msi_reset is true, and to 1 when msr_read is true, combined with MSR assignment that forces delta field to 4'b0 when msi_reset is true else ORs prior value with modem change XOR.
- **Proposed test:** Test async wb_rst_i assert/deassert for msi_reset init value and self-clear timing; test msr_read pulse width and that delta bits clear on next clk; test back-to-back reads and modem toggle in same cycle as read.
- **Specification comparison:** DOCUMENTED_IN_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Is msi_reset intended to be 1 after wb_rst_i, self-clear to 0 in one clk, and re-assert for one clk on msr_read to clear MSR delta bits, and what is the required read-to-clear latency versus concurrent modem-input changes?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (8 excerpts)
  - lines 458-468
  - lines 460
  - lines 461
  - lines 463
  - lines 464
  - lines 466
  - lines 467
  - lines 582-583

### RTLOBS-82e64dc1b8 — reset ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

FCR-controlled rx_reset/tx_reset appear as single-cycle auto-clearing pulses: set from write data only in the FCR-write cycle, otherwise forced to 0, with async reset forcing 0.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived from shared always block on posedge clk/posedge wb_rst_i where reset branch forces both resets to 0, FCR-write branch loads them from wb_dat_i bits, and else branch forces them to 0, indicating pulse rather than level control.
- **Proposed test:** Test FCR writes with 01/10/11 combinations for pulse width and self-clear; test no-write cycles hold 0; test async wb_rst_i during asserted pulse and overlapping FCR writes; test downstream FIFO/shift-register clear versus pulse.
- **Specification comparison:** NOT_FOUND_IN_RETRIEVED_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Are rx_reset and tx_reset intended as single-cycle pulses loaded from wb_dat_i[1]/[2] on FCR writes and auto-cleared to 0 otherwise, with async wb_rst_i forcing 0, and how long must they remain asserted to reliably clear receiver/transmitter FIFOs?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (8 excerpts)
  - lines 500-513
  - lines 501
  - lines 503
  - lines 504
  - lines 508
  - lines 509
  - lines 511
  - lines 512

### RTLOBS-b317862303 — integration ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Modem-status delta path has order-sensitive integration: top bundles modem_inputs as cts/dsr/ri/dcd while MSR logic evaluates dcd/ri/dsr/cts XOR delayed signals.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived by comparing top instantiation concatenating modem inputs as cts,dsr,ri,dcd with MSR update that XORs dcd,ri,dsr,cts against delayed_modem_signals[3:0], requiring order/polarity review as static graph cannot confirm bit mapping.
- **Proposed test:** Drive each modem pin individually through synchronized path and check which MSR delta/current bit toggles and that msi_reset clears correct bits; test simultaneous toggles and reset-vs-toggle corner.
- **Specification comparison:** NOT_FOUND_IN_RETRIEVED_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** What is the intended bit correspondence between top-level {cts_pad_i,dsr_pad_i,ri_pad_i,dcd_pad_i} modem_inputs order and MSR delta expression {dcd,ri,dsr,cts} ^ delayed_modem_signals[3:0], including which physical pin maps to which MSR delta bit?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_top.v (1 excerpt)
  - lines 268-302
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (1 excerpt)
  - lines 582-583

### RTLOBS-d4ddb2cf8b — clocking ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Baud enable flop is reset to 0 and combinationally gated by divisor-latch state, asserting only when divisor is non-zero and counter is zero.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived from always block on posedge clk/posedge wb_rst_i that forces enable to 0 on reset and otherwise selects 1 only for |dl & ~(|dlc) and 0 otherwise, a control gating candidate feeding serial engines.
- **Proposed test:** Test reset value, DL=0 case, DL>0 with dlc zero vs non-zero, and divisor reload sequence for enable gating and start of transmission/reception; monitor for unintended clock-enable gaps.
- **Specification comparison:** NOT_FOUND_IN_RETRIEVED_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Is enable intended to be 1 only when divisor latch is non-zero and divisor counter is zero (|dl & ~(|dlc)), forced 0 on wb_rst_i, and what is expected behavior for DL=0 or during divisor reload?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (2 excerpts)
  - lines 704-713
  - lines 706

### RTLOBS-4574763f90 — dependency ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

LSR bit path includes a one-cycle delay flop lsr1_d that tracks lsr1 and is asynchronously cleared by wb_rst_i.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived from always block on posedge clk/posedge wb_rst_i that assigns lsr1_d to 0 on reset else to lsr1, indicating a pipeline delay whose consumer timing affects status/interrupt visibility.
- **Proposed test:** Test reset clear, one-cycle delay from lsr1 toggle to lsr1_d, and effect on LSR read data and line-status interrupt generation/clear; test back-to-back error events.
- **Specification comparison:** NOT_FOUND_IN_RETRIEVED_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Is lsr1_d intended as a one-cycle delayed copy of lsr1 with async clear to 0, and which LSR read/interrupt path depends on the delayed versus immediate version?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (3 excerpts)
  - lines 617-619
  - lines 618
  - lines 619

### RTLOBS-fa2cb00ca3 — integration ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

DTR output is a combinational assign from MCR passed through the top, with no evidenced registered reset state.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Specification comparison:** NOT_FOUND_IN_RETRIEVED_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)

### RTLOBS-17759db7e0 — dependency ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Receiver-to-regs handshake wires rx_reset inward and rf_push_pulse/rf_overrun outward, coupling FIFO push and overrun handling to reset and enable.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Prioritize reset behavior and configuration setup before traffic, then error reporting and modem-status handling with loopback as the primary data-path vehicle. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Use a fixed system-clock period per test with directed and seeded random checks once limits are confirmed, treating RTL observations as review-dependent risks. 📄<!--dv-sources:W3siaWQiOiAiQ0gtNjNhZDRkNjFhNSIsICJ3aGVyZSI6ICJ1YXJ0MTY1NTAvZG9jL1VBUlRfc3BlYy5wZGYsIHAuNiIsICJzdW1tYXJ5IjogIjIuMSBXSVNIQk9ORSBpbnRlcmZhY2Ugc2lnbmFscyBQb3J0IFdpZHRoIERpcmVjdGlvbiBEZXNjcmlwdGlvbiBDTEsgMSBJbnB1dCBCbG9ja-KAmXMgY2xvY2sgaW5wdXQgV0JfUlNUX0kgMSBJbnB1dCBBc3luY2hyb25vdXMgUmVzZXQgV0JfQUREUl9JIDUgb3IgMyBJbnB1dCBVc2VkIGZvciByZWdpc3RlciBzZWxlY3Rpb24gV0JfU0VMX0kgNCBJbnB1dCBTZWxlY3Qgc2lnbmFsIFdCX0RBVF9JIDMyIG9yIDggSW5wdXQgRGF0In1d-->

### Sequence Implementation

  - Knobs: DLAB-gated access, divisor MSB/LSB, LCR format, FCR trigger, IER enables, MCR loopback.
  - Ordering: run after power_on_reset and uart_config; virtual sequences coordinate reset then configure then traffic.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Implement serial_traffic in serial_data sequencer to drive SRX_PAD_I and observe STX_PAD_O across line formats. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes traffic sequence to produce documented send/receive behavior; randomization and field choice are methodology.
  - Owning agent/sequencer: serial_data active agent sequencer.
  - Transaction fields: serial byte payload, LCR character length, parity, stop bits, divisor-derived baud timing.
  - Stimulus: directed 8-bit no-parity 1-stop plus constrained-random lengths, parity modes, break and error injection.
  - Ordering: start only after divisor programmed and transmission engine enabled; coordinate with wishbone_reg_access via virtual sequences.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Implement modem_handshake in modem_control sequencer to drive modem inputs and MCR controls including loopback. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes handshake sequence for documented modem control and status; stimulus method is a methodology choice.
  - Owning agent/sequencer: modem_control active agent sequencer.
  - Transaction fields: MCR DTR/RTS/Out1/Out2/loopback controls and CTS/DSR/RI/DCD inputs.
  - Stimulus: directed per-pin toggles plus constrained-random simultaneous toggles and loopback entry/exit.
  - Ordering: program MCR in uart_config before loopback_traffic; toggle modem inputs during normal_traffic_with_modem_interrupt.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Implement clock_gen and reset_seq with power_on_reset virtual sequence coordinating clock, reset, wishbone_bus, serial_data and modem_control bring-up. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes generator ownership and fixed-period ordering for documented reset tasks; coordination is methodology.
  - clock_gen in sys_clock drives CLK with fixed period per test; reset_seq in sys_reset drives WB_RST_I assert/deassert.
  - Order: clock stable, then reset assert, then deassert, then idle register/pin check before uart_config.
  - Sequence timing and reset duration scale with selected CLK period.
  - No dynamic period change during reset or traffic.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Implement uart_config virtual sequence programming LCR, divisor latches, FIFO trigger and IER enables in dependency order. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes virtual-sequence programming order from documented initialization steps; sequencing is methodology.
  - Prerequisite: set LCR bit 7 to 1 to allow divisor access, then program MSB first LSB next.
  - Then clear LCR bit 7 to 0 to return to normal registers before FIFO and IER programming.

  - Produces: configured divisor and line state for predictors and scoreboards.

  - Inference: Proposes traffic families to exercise documented FIFO, trigger and interrupt behavior; family partition is methodology.

### Check Implementation

-  Expect receiver and transmitter FIFOs cleared upon reset. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Trigger: after WB_RST_I deassert and after FCR clear commands.
  - Expected: empty FIFOs before initialization traffic.
  - Failure: any stale data readable or write/read mismatch due to uncleared state reported as reset failure.
-  Expect Line Control Register reset to 8 bits data, no parity, 1 stop bit. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Trigger: register readback after reset before uart_config.
  - Expected: 8 bits data, no parity, 1 stop bit configuration.
  - Failure: any other LCR decode reported as reset-value failure.
-  Expect Divisor Latch register set to 0 upon reset. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Trigger: divisor readback with DLAB set after reset.
  - Expected: divisor zero before programming.
  - Failure: non-zero divisor reported as reset-value failure; baud behavior with zero divisor is designer question.

> LSB.(whole register) note: Specification states no enumerated values for divisor LSB. Verification programs via wishbone_bus in uart_config with DLAB set, MSB first then LSB, then clears DLAB to start engine. Reset value 0.
> Divisor Latch Byte 2.(whole register) note: Specification states no enumerated values for divisor MSB. Verification programs via wishbone_bus in uart_config with DLAB set, MSB first then LSB, then clears DLAB to start engine. Reset value 0.
> IER.Received Data available interrupt note: Enables Received Data available interrupt. Reset disables all interrupts. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> IER.Received Data available interrupt inference: Randomization weighting chosen to cover documented enable-disable interrupt behavior through uart_config and traffic sequences.
> IER.Transmitter Holding Register empty interrupt note: Enables Transmitter Holding Register empty interrupt. Reset disables all interrupts. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> IER.Transmitter Holding Register empty interrupt inference: Randomization weighting chosen to cover documented enable-disable interrupt behavior through uart_config and traffic sequences.
> IER.Receiver Line Status Interrupt note: Enables Receiver Line Status interrupt. Reset disables all interrupts. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> IER.Receiver Line Status Interrupt inference: Randomization weighting chosen to cover documented enable-disable interrupt behavior through uart_config and traffic sequences.
> IER.Modem Status Interrupt note: Enables Modem Status interrupt. Reset disables all interrupts. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> IER.Modem Status Interrupt inference: Randomization weighting chosen to cover documented enable-disable interrupt behavior through uart_config and traffic sequences.
> IER.Reserved note: Reserved field required to be logic 0. Verification holds at 0 while randomizing IER enable bits.
> FCR. note: Specification states bit is ignored with FIFO only operation. No enumerated values stated. Verification keeps at reset value.
> FCR. note: Specification states bits are ignored. No enumerated values stated. Verification keeps at reset value.
> FCR. note: Defines Receiver FIFO interrupt trigger level for 1, 4, 8, 14 bytes. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> FCR. inference: Coverage weighting chosen to exercise documented trigger thresholds and recommended 14-byte setting through uart_config.
> LCR.Select number of bits in each character note: Selects 5, 6, 7, 8 bits per character. Reset selects 8 bits. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config before divisor.
> LCR.Select number of bits in each character inference: Random sweep chosen to cover documented character lengths through uart_config and serial_traffic.
> LCR.Specify the number of generated stop bits note: Specifies 1 stop bit or 1.5 or 2 stop bits. Reset selects 1 stop bit. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> LCR.Specify the number of generated stop bits inference: Random sweep chosen to cover documented stop-bit dependency on character length through serial_traffic.
> LCR.Parity Enable note: Enables parity generation and checking. Reset selects no parity. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> LCR.Parity Enable inference: Randomization chosen to cover documented parity generation and checking on outgoing and incoming characters.
> LCR.Even Parity select note: Selects odd or even number of 1s transmitted and checked. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> LCR.Even Parity select inference: Random sweep chosen to cover documented odd versus even parity selection through serial_traffic.
> LCR.Stick Parity bit. note: Controls stick parity disabled or forced parity handling. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> LCR.Stick Parity bit. inference: Random sweep chosen to cover documented stick parity mode through uart_config and error_recovery sequences.
> LCR.Break Control bit note: When 1 serial out forced to 0 break state, when 0 break disabled. Used in serial_traffic and error_recovery.
> LCR.Break Control bit inference: Distribution chosen to cover documented break forcing of serial out while keeping normal traffic dominant.
> LCR.Divisor Latch Access bit. note: Divisor Latch Access bit selects divisor or normal registers. Toggled via wishbone_bus in uart_config.
> LCR.Divisor Latch Access bit. inference: Control sequencing chosen to implement documented divisor versus normal access routing in uart_config.
> MCR.Data Terminal Ready (DTR) signal control note: Controls DTR output level. Program via wishbone_bus with observation on modem_control monitor.

> MCR.Request To Send (RTS) signal control note: Controls RTS output level. Program via wishbone_bus with observation on modem_control monitor.
> MCR.Request To Send (RTS) signal control inference: Random toggle chosen to exercise documented RTS output control through modem_handshake.

> MCR.Loopback mode note: Selects normal operation or loopback mode. Program via wishbone_bus in uart_config and modem_handshake.

### Reuse

- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Share wishbone_bus active agent, wishbone_bus monitor and wishbone_reg_access plus uart_config and power_on_reset virtual sequences with SoC testbench for register access. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

  - Applies to WISHBONE slave responder access through the interconnect.
  - Preserves DLAB-gated divisor versus normal routing with MSB-first LSB-next order from uart_config.
  - Includes power_on_reset coordination of clock, reset and bus bring-up.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Share serial_data and modem_control active agents with serial_traffic, modem_handshake, loopback_traffic and normal_traffic_with_modem_interrupt sequences with SoC testbench for external-pin traffic. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes sharing serial and modem stimulus at SoC; sharing scope is an engineering choice beyond the spec.
  - Peer types are modem or other external devices over serial link.
  - Preserves loopback_traffic internal return and normal traffic with modem activity.
  - Uses modem_handshake for DTR, RTS, Out1 and Out2 controls.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Share wishbone_bus, serial_data, modem_control, uart_interrupt and baud_output monitors with register predictor and data-path scoreboards with SoC testbench for observation. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes sharing passive observation and scoreboards at SoC; sharing scope is an engineering choice beyond the spec.
  - Preserves wishbone_bus transaction reconstruction and serial frame reconstruction.
  - Passive INT_O observation with IER and IIR expectation remains in modem_interrupt_scoreboard.
  - Passive baud observation remains without driving.

-  Confirm WISHBONE slave responder connectivity to SoC interconnect for address decode, control handling and acknowledge return. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

  - SoC confirms bus fabric timing and acknowledge latency.
-  Confirm serial transmit and receive pad connectivity from UART core to SoC pins. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

-  Confirm modem handshake signal integration including optional implementation through general-purpose I/Os. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

  - NEEDS_REVIEW: RTL design engineer approval required.
  - Drive each modem pin individually through synchronized path and check toggled MSR delta and current bits.

  - NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer for intended pin-to-bit correspondence.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Confirm DTR output value during reset and MCR writes at SoC pad level. NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

  - NEEDS_REVIEW: RTL design engineer approval required.

  - NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer for intended reset value and registered behavior.
### Verify At Higher Level

-  Defer RS232 serial-link behavior with modem or other external devices to SoC and system level with cable and peer model. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

## 12. Assumptions

_Provenance: unmarked facts are documented; ⚠️ marks inference and 🛑 marks assumed or unreferenced content. Heading links collect documented sources. 📄 hovers source excerpts._


### Assumption

- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume CLK from the WISHBONE bus is driven at a fixed period within each test chosen to satisfy the divisor to baud relationship for serial traffic. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - sys_clock is treated as infrastructure source with constant period after power_on_reset.
  - wishbone_bus and serial_data timing are checked against the selected period.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume WB_RST_I is an active-high asynchronous reset held long enough by power_on_reset to clear FIFOs and shift registers before uart_config programs registers. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Programming follows reset clear then line control, divisor latch MSB first LSB next, trigger level and interrupt enable order.
  - wishbone_bus agent stays idle while reset is asserted.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume the WISHBONE slave responder returns WB_ACK_O for each qualified WB_STB_I with WB_CYC_I access in the selected build with WB_SEL_I qualifying the accessed byte. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - wishbone_bus active agent and wishbone_reg_access sequence model single acknowledge return.
  - Address decode is assumed stable during strobe for documented registers.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume receiver and transmitter FIFOs are empty after reset and that the trigger level set by uart_config remains reachable during serial_traffic. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Data-path scoreboards start from empty state after reset clear.
  - Recommendation of 14 bytes is assumed as a reachable trigger setting for interrupt checks.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume the serial line idles high and that after reset the character format is 8 data bits with no parity and 1 stop bit until uart_config reprograms the line control. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - serial_data agent with serial_traffic and loopback_traffic models idle-high framing.
  - Compatibility with NS16550A framing is assumed for start and stop behavior.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume INT_O is observed passively and stays asserted while any enabled interrupt source is pending until cleared by its documented register access. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - uart_interrupt monitor with modem_interrupt_scoreboard checks persistence against IER gating.
  - IIR bit 0 low is assumed to mean pending with priority decode per interrupt type.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume BAUD_O when implemented is a passive 16x baud-rate output that is only observed and never driven by the testbench. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - baud_output monitor records toggling without driving.
  - No baud accuracy check is assumed beyond observation of enable versus divisor setting.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume modem status delta bits clear to zero on the clock after MSR read and test back-to-back reads with a modem toggle in the same cycle as read NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes read-to-clear timing check because spec lists modem-status reset control as MSR read without defining pulse latency.
  - NEEDS_REVIEW: RTL design engineer approval required.
  - modem_control agent drives individual CTS, DSR, RI and DCD toggles through modem_handshake.
  - Check MSR delta and current bits with msi_reset behavior proposed from observation.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume FCR FIFO reset controls act as single-cycle pulses that self-clear when no FCR write occurs and test overlapping writes and reset during pulse NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes pulse-width stimulus because spec only states FIFOs are cleared without defining FCR reset assertion length.
  - NEEDS_REVIEW: RTL design engineer approval required.
  - wishbone_reg_access drives 01, 10 and 11 combinations to FIFO control.
  - Check downstream FIFO and shift-register clear versus pulse width.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume no baud enable or serial transmission occurs with divisor latch at zero and that enable asserts only with non-zero divisor and zero counter NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Derives zero-divisor gating check from reset-to-zero divisor and baud formula without defined zero behavior.
  - NEEDS_REVIEW: RTL design engineer approval required.
  - uart_config programs divisor MSB first LSB next then checks start of serial_traffic.
  - baud_output monitor checks for absence of toggling at zero divisor versus toggling after reload.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume line-status path includes a one-cycle delayed copy affecting LSR read and interrupt generation and test back-to-back error events NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes delay-aware interrupt check because spec lists line-status sources without defining delayed versus immediate path.
  - NEEDS_REVIEW: RTL design engineer approval required.
  - serial_data agent injects parity, framing and overrun errors via serial_traffic.
  - Check LSR read data and line-status interrupt timing against delayed version.
- ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume receiver push and overrun indications couple to FIFO write with reset clearing both without losing a concurrent push NEEDS_REVIEW by RTL design engineer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Inference: Proposes concurrent push-reset stimulus because spec only states data can be sent and received without defining handshake timing.
  - NEEDS_REVIEW: RTL design engineer approval required.
  - serial_data agent drives FIFO-full plus concurrent pop with push modeling in scoreboard.
  - Check overrun set and clear with rx_reset asserted during push and enable gating.

## 13. Questions to Designers ✅<!--dv-evidence:-->

_Provenance: unmarked facts are documented; ⚠️ marks inference and 🛑 marks assumed or unreferenced content. Heading links collect documented sources. 📄 hovers source excerpts._


### Question

-  What is the expected WISHBONE write and read behavior for IER bits 7-4 when written to 1, including whether they are stored, returned on read, or affect interrupt generation? 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Reset value is 00h with all enables disabled.
  - Clarify handling required by uart_config for reserved-bit writes and read return value.
-  How does each IER enable bit gate interrupt generation and clearing, including which register access clears each pending source? 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Includes received data available, transmitter holding register empty, receiver line status and modem status sources.
  - Clarify INT_O assertion, priority and clearing through wishbone_bus and uart_interrupt observation.
-  What is the expected WISHBONE read value and write side effect for FCR, including whether clear bits 1-2 self-clear and whether ignored bits are stored? 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Bits 5-3 and bit 0 are described as Ignored.
  - Clarify read return value for write-only FCR via wishbone_reg_access.
-  Does FCR reset value 11000000b intend a default 14-byte receiver trigger level, and does writing trigger bits alone disturb FIFO contents or shift registers? 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Trigger encodings listed as 00 1 byte, 01 4 bytes, 10 8 bytes and 11 14 bytes.
  - Clear description states the shift register is not cleared.
-  What is the complete definition for LCR stick parity when bits 3 and 4 are logic 1 and for any unspecified upper LCR bits, since the description ends mid-sentence? 📄<!--dv-sources:-->

### Reference CH-0174a058ac

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.15

> 4.8 Modem Status Register (MSR)
> 
> The register displays the current state of the modem control lines. Also, four bits also
> provide an indication in the state of one of the modem status lines. These bits are set to
> ‘1’ when a change in corresponding line has been detected and they are reset when the
> register is being read.
> 
> Bit # Access Description
> 0 R Delta Clear To Send (DCTS) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The CTS line has changed its state.
> 1 R Delta Data Set Ready (DDSR) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The DSR line has changed its state.
> 2 R Trailing Edge of Ring Indicator  (TERI) detector. The RI line has
> changed its state from low to high state.
> 3 R Delta Data Carrier De tect (DDCD) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The DCD line has changed its state.
> 4 R Complement of the CTS input or equals to RTS in loopback mode.
> 5 R Complement of the DSR input or equals to DTR in loopback mode.
> 6 R Complement of the RI input or equals to Out1 in loopback mode.
> 7 R Complement of the DCD input or equals to Out2 in loopback mode.

### Reference CH-06bad6ffcd

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.15

> 4.9 Divisor Latches
> 
> The divisor latches can be accessed by setting the 7th bit of LCR to ‘1’. You should
> restore this bit to ‘0’ after setting the divisor latches in order to restore access to the other
> registers that occupy the same addresses. The 2 bytes form one 16-bit register, which is
> internally accessed as a single number. You should therefore set all 2 bytes of the register
> to ensure normal operation. The register is set to the default value of 0 on reset, which
> disables all serial I/O operations in order to ensure explicit setup of the register in the
> software. The value set should be equal to (system clock speed) / (16 x desired baud rate).
> The internal counter starts to work when the LSB of DL is written, so when setting the
> divisor, write the MSB first and the LSB last.
> 

### Reference CH-1e2324cfc3

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.17

> 5.1 Initialization
> 
> Upon reset the core performs the following tasks:
> 
> • The receiver and transmitter FIFOs are cleared.
> • The receiver and transmitter shift registers are cleared
> • The Divisor Latch register is set to 0.
> • The Line Control Register is set to communication of 8 bits of data, no parity, 1
> stop bit.
> • All interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register.
> 
> For proper operation, perform the following:
> 
> • Set the Line Control Register to the desired line control parameters. Set bit 7 to ‘1’
> to allow access to the Divisor Latches.
> • Set the Divisor Latches, MSB first, LSB next.
> • Set bit 7 of LCR to ‘0’ to disable access to Divisor Latches. At this time the
> transmission engine starts working and data can be sent and received.
> • Set the FIFO trigger level. Generally, higher trigger level values produce less
> interrupt to the system, so setting it to 14 bytes is recommended if the system

### Reference CH-2baa4497c0

> 1
> Introduction
> 
> The UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) core provides serial
> communication capabilities, which allow communication with modem or other external
> devices, like another computer using a serial cable and RS232 protocol. This core is
> designed to be maximally compatible with the industry standard National
> Semiconductors’ 16550A device.
> 
> Features:
> 
> • WISHBONE interface in 32-bit or 8-bit data bus modes (selectable)
> • FIFO only operation
> • Register level and functionality compatibility with NS16550A (but not 16450).
> • Debug Interface in 32-bit data bus mode.

### Reference CH-419b99d7d8

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.17

> 5
> Operation
> 
> This UART core is very similar in operation to the standard 16550 UART chip with the
> main exception being that only the FIFO mode is supported. The scratch register is
> removed, as it serves no purpose.
> 
> This core can operate in 8-bit data bus mode or in 32-bit bus mode, which is now the
> default mode.
> 
> The 32-bit mode is fully WISHBONE compatible and it uses the WISHBONE [SEL_I]
> signal to properly receive and return 8-bit data on 32-bit data bus. The 8-bit version might
> have problems in various WISHBONE implementations because a 32-bit master reading
> from 8-bit bus can expect data on different bytes of the 4-byte word, depending on the
> register address.
> Also, in 32-bit data bus mode, the [ADR_I] is 5 and not 3 bits wide.
> 
> In addition, in the 32-bit data bus mode a debug interface is present in the system. This
> interface has 2 32-bit registers that can be read to provide non-intrusive look into the
> core’s registers and other internal values of importance.

### Reference CH-6abe65aeff

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.13

> 4.6 Modem Control Register (MCR)
> 
> The modem control register allows transferring control signals to a modem connected to
> the UART.
> 
> Bit # Access Description
> 0 W Data Terminal Ready (DTR) signal control
>  ‘0’ – DTR is ‘1’
>  ‘1’ – DTR is ‘0’
> 1 W Request To Send (RTS) signal control
>  ‘0’ – RTS is ‘1’
>  ‘1’ – RTS is ‘0’
> 2 W Out1. In loopback mode, connected Ring Indicator (RI) signal input
> 3 W Out2. In loopback mode, connected to Data Carrier Detect (DCD)
> input.

> 4.7 Line Status Register (LSR)
> 
> Bit # Access Description
> 0 R Data Ready (DR) indicator.
>  ‘0’ – No characters in the FIFO
>  ‘1’ – At least one character has been received and is in the
> FIFO.
> 1 R Overrun Error (OE) indicator
>  ‘1’ – If the FIFO is full and another character has been
> received in the receiver shift register. If another character is starting
> to arrive, it will overwrite the data in the shift register but the FIFO
> will remain intact. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register.
> Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.
>  ‘0’ – No overrun state
> 2 R Parity Error (PE) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The character that is currently at the top of the FIFO
> has been received with parity error. The bit is cleared upon reading
> from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.
>  ‘0’ – No parity error in the current character
> 3 R Framing Error (FE) indicator

### Reference CH-dfb1048908

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.11

> 4.4 FIFO Control Register (FCR)
> 
> The FCR allows selection of the FIFO trigger level (the number of bytes in FIFO required
> to enable the Received Data Available interrupt).  In addition, the FIFOs can be cleared
> using this register.
> 
> Bit # Access Description
> 0 W Ignored (Used to enable FIFOs in NS16550D). Since this UART
> only supports FIFO mode, this bit is ignored.
> 1 W Writing a ‘1’ to bit 1 clears the Receiver FIFO and resets its logic.
> But it doesn’t clear the shift register, i.e. receiving of the current
> character continues.
> 2 W Writing a ‘1’ to bit 2 clears the Transmitter FIFO and resets its
> logic. The shift register is not cleared, i.e. transmitting of the
> current character continues.
> 5-3 W Ignored
> 7-6 W Define the Receiver FIFO Interrupt trigger level
>  ‘00’ – 1 byte
>  ‘01’ – 4 bytes
>  ‘10’ – 8 bytes
